A.explanation: Too small because it counts only one side of the pattern or uses $n_{max}$ without adding the zero order and the symmetric orders.

B.explanation: Too small because it is close to $d/\lambda \approx 4.8$ but forgets to include maxima on both sides of the zero order.

C.explanation: One short of the full count because it uses $2n_{max}$ for $n_{max}=4$ but omits the central $n=0$ maximum.

D.explanation: Correct because $n_{max}=4$ on each side plus the zero order gives $2 \times 4 + 1 = 9$ maxima.

hints: Convert the 300 lines per mm into the grating spacing $d$ in metres using $d = 10^{-3}/300 \text{ m}$.
Use the grating equation $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ with $\lambda = 690 \text{ nm}$ and set $\sin\theta = 1$ for the largest possible angle.
Remember the curved screen shows orders on both sides, so add the $+n$ orders, the $-n$ orders and the $n=0$ central maximum.
walkthrough: Find the slit spacing from 300 lines per mm: $d = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3}}{300} = 3.33 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
Write the diffraction grating condition $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ with $\lambda = 690 \text{ nm} = 690 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.
The highest order occurs at the largest $\sin\theta = 1$, so $n_{max} = d/\lambda$.
Substitute values: $n_{max} = \frac{3.33 \times 10^{-6}}{690 \times 10^{-9}} \approx 4.83$, so only integer orders up to $n = 4$ are possible.
Count all visible maxima: central $n=0$ plus $n = 1,2,3,4$ on each side, giving $2 \times 4 + 1 = 9$. This is option D.
